# AEM Source Designer

The **AEM Source Designer** toolbox uses the Analytic Element Method to describe a
contaminant source and estimate transport parameters. It complements the closed-form
analytical models by letting you lay out a source geometry explicitly and then run
the transport problem forward, or invert field observations for the parameters that
best reproduce them.

The toolbox has three parts:

## 1. Designer

Lay out the source interactively on a canvas: place and edit source elements, set the
model parameters (longitudinal / transverse dispersivity $\alpha_L$, $\alpha_T$,
source concentration $c_A$, decay $\gamma$, source width $W_s$) and the computational
parameters (grid increment, control points, expansion terms, plot aspect). The
designer reports the maximum plume length $L_{max}$ for the configured source.

::: {.callout-note}
The source elements must stay a small clearance below the water table for the
solution to be valid; the designer flags configurations that violate this.
:::

## 2. Forward simulation

Run the configured source forward to produce the steady-state plume and its
$L_{max}$, drawn together with a reference line at the computed maximum extent.

## 3. Inverse estimation

Given field observations, scan the parameter space to estimate the source and
transport parameters that best reproduce the observed plume — a parameter-estimation
/ optimization workflow rather than a single forward run.

## When to use it

Reach for the AEM Source Designer when a single closed-form source (a patch or point)
is too simplistic for your site, when you need an explicit source geometry, or when
you want to **estimate** parameters from observations instead of assuming them.
